Solution 2 is the only one whose answer, 171, matches my analysis. Ana can separate primes p and q only if the bipartite graph linking residues mod p and mod q (with the queried points as edges) is connected, and at most one prime can have an unqueried residue class. Since at least two of {83, 89, 97} must be fully covered, the bipartite connectivity bound forces n ≥ 171. I did not verify that 171 points can satisfy every pair simultaneously, so the upper bound is plausible but not confirmed.
